    The special product underlying the BGRS ray category #

    For morphisms μ : X ⟶ Y and ν : Y ⟶ Z, BGRS does not always compose their unit rays by taking the ray of μ ≫ ν. The product is the zero ray when the composite is already obtained by inserting an element of the Jacobson radical of the middle endomorphism ring. This file records that test, the representative-level product, and the exact laws needed for it to descend to a category of rays.

    The laws are proved later from distributivity of the concrete primitive- projective category. Keeping them explicit here prevents the unit-orbit projection from being mistaken for a functor or an ordinary categorical quotient.

            class LargeIndecomposable.HasWellDefinedBGRSRayProduct (C : Type u) [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] :
            Prop

            The exact operational laws needed for the representative-level BGRS product to define a category on two-sided unit rays.

            For the concrete primitive-projective category these laws are consequences of distributivity. They are kept as a named boundary rather than silently assuming that ordinary composition descends to unit orbits.

            • congr {W X Y : C} {f f' : W ⟶ X} {g g' : X ⟶ Y} : UnitRayEquivalent f f' → UnitRayEquivalent g g' → UnitRayEquivalent (bgrsRayRepresentativeProduct f g) (bgrsRayRepresentativeProduct f' g')
